subject: Private K8s delivery: fleet constraints and storage orchestration proposal
body:
From: Carla Diaz <carla.diaz@acme-telemetry.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-telemetry.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Private K8s delivery: fleet constraints and storage orchestration proposal

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The execs asked us to move faster on an on‑prem private deployment for our inference workload. We put together the attached site inventory and a short wish list: low-latency NVMe local SSD for model KV cache, a small HA etcd footprint, and per-tenant PVC isolation.

Can your team review our inventory and sketch a recommended node fleet and storage orchestration approach? Our constraints: two racks per site, limited cross-rack bandwidth (10 Gbps uplinks), air-gapped deploys on some customers, and strict audit logging requirements.

Appreciate an initial take and a call to align.

—Carla
VP, Edge Platforms
Acme Telemetry

----

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Carla Diaz <carla.diaz@acme-telemetry.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 13:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Private K8s delivery: fleet constraints and storage orchestration proposal

Hi Carla —

Thanks for the inventory (received). Quick read: we can accommodate NVMe local caching and per-tenant PVCs but need to make trade-offs for HA and cross-rack traffic. High-level suggestions before we deep-dive:

- Node fleet: separate node pools for inference (GPU/accelerators), cache-heavy workers (local NVMe), control-plane (etcd + ops) and stock ephemeral workers. Prefer isolated taints/tolerations to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
- Storage: use local NVMe for KV cache with a write-through to an encrypted object store for persistence. For stateful components (etcd), recommend 3-node etcd spread across racks with dedicated low-latency NICs and static routes.
- Networking: enable per-pod egress policy and an egress gateway to minimize cross-rack chattiness. Where uplink is constrained, we can enable compression for inter-node replication traffic.
- Air-gapped: we support a private bundle for on-site install; will need SRE to validate offline KMS key provisioning.

Next steps: I propose a 45-min technical review with your infra and security leads. Marissa — can you pick two deployment diagrams (one for single-rack minimal, one for two-rack HA) and a recommended node fleet matrix? Karthik/Jonas, please flag any known limitations around etcd placements and network QoS.

Available windows: Thu 09/09 09:30–11:00 ET or Fri 09/10 14:00–16:00 ET.

—Sofia
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

----

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Carla Diaz <carla.diaz@acme-telemetry.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 09:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Private K8s delivery: fleet constraints and storage orchestration proposal

Carla / Sofia —

I attached two artifacts: a proposed node-fleet matrix (proposed-node-fleet-matrix.pdf) and a hand-drawn network egress zones export (network-egress-zones.drawio.png). Key points from my read:

- Minimal (single-rack): 1 control-plane (3 etcd instances as static pods on 3 physically separate hosts if available), 3 inference GPU nodes, 2 cache nodes (NVMe), 2 general workers. This reduces cross-rack replication but accepts single-rack failure risk.
- HA (two-rack): spread etcd across racks (2+1 quorum) with private replication VLANs. Use local NVMe on cache nodes and enable asynchronous replication to our object store during off-peak windows.
- Storage orchestration: leverage longhorn/rook for PV abstraction if customer allows CSI drivers; otherwise we recommend operator-driven local provisioner with snapshotting to S3-compatible object store.
- Security: ensure KMS integration for disk encryption keys and enable audit forwarders to your SIEM.

Open questions for Acme:
1) Can you confirm whether CSI drivers are permitted in the air-gapped sites?
2) Do you have a preferred S3 endpoint for offsite persistence (name/IP)?
3) What are the expected QPS and model sizes (RAM+KV working set) for inference nodes?

I can present these diagrams on the call. Sofia — I tentatively booked Thu 09/09 10:00 ET with the Acme calendar invite; please confirm.

—Marissa
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-node-fleet-matrix.pdf, network-egress-zones.drawio.png

----

From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme-telemetry.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Carla Diaz <carla.diaz@acme-telemetry.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2027 16:20:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Private K8s delivery: fleet constraints and storage orchestration proposal

Marissa/Sofia —

10:00 ET works for us; thanks for pulling the matrix together. Quick answers inline:

1) CSI drivers: allowed on non-air-gapped sites. For air-gapped, we require a vendor-approved offline bundle; we can allow Rook only if the image artifacts are pre-approved.
2) S3 endpoint: s3.acme-telemetry.internal (we'll send network allowlist ahead of the call).
3) QPS/model: baseline 120 QPS across 3 hot models, each model ~6GB resident + ~20GB KV cache working set. We'll bring detailed telemetry on the call.

On the call we want to validate: expected failover behavior for node loss, PVC reclamation during upgrades, and audit/logging placement to avoid hotspots. See you at 10.

—Tom
Infra Lead, Acme Telemetry
